mainTopic: Minimum and maximum limits: a טועה's clean days, quarantine for נגעים, full months, the Temple breads and מילה
overview: This amud first finishes a ברייתא's list of how many clean days a טועה must count before her doubt ends (her פתח). The list closes with a rule: her פתח is never fewer than seven clean days and never more than seventeen. רב אדא בר אהבה asks why she can't just count seven clean days. רבה answers that the counting is not about permitting her to her husband but about putting her back on a clear נדה cycle. A ברייתא then teaches that uncertain זבות bring a קרבן that is not eaten, except in the seven-day and eight-day פתח cases, and the גמרא rereads its wording. A new משנה says quarantine for נגעים lasts from one week (נגעי אדם) to three weeks (נגעי בתים). רב פפא ties this to the פסוק 'צדקתך כהררי אל', which leads to a dispute between רב יהודה and רבה about its plain meaning, rooted in whether God כובש or נושא. Finally, a משנה lists more minimums and maximums: full months in a year, the שתי הלחם, the לחם הפנים and מילה. The גמרא begins explaining why no more than eight months are made full, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Twelve days of blood means eight clean days; thirteen means seven
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. If she saw blood for twelve days, her פתח comes after eight clean days. If she saw blood for thirteen days, it comes after seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says 'I saw twelve days,' her opening comes after eight clean days. If she says 'thirteen days,' her opening comes after seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from a ברייתא. Each line says how many clean days a woman needs before her doubt ends, depending on how many days she saw blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא always assumes the worst case: the bleeding may have started at the end of her ימי זיבה and run into her נדה days and beyond. The more days she bled, the further into the cycle she has already gone. So the number of clean days still needed to finish the cycle keeps going down: twelve days of bleeding leaves eight clean days, and thirteen leaves seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Her 'opening': the point after which her doubt is over and a new cycle clearly begins
A woman who has lost track of whether she is in her נדה days or her זיבה days
The eleven days after the seven days of נדה, when bleeding can make her a זבה

steps.confusionAlert: The numbers go DOWN as the bleeding days go UP. That is not a mistake. More days of bleeding means more of the cycle is already used up, so fewer clean days are left to count.

phrases.english: If she says 'twelve' — her opening is eight.
phrases.notes: 'Her opening' means the point where her doubt ends. Here that is after eight clean days.

phrases.english: If she says 'thirteen' — her opening is seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list from the previous section, adding the last two entries.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twelve days of bleeding means eight clean days. Thirteen days of bleeding means seven clean days.

steps.title: The general rule: between seven and seventeen clean days
steps.stepSummary: Summing up the list: a טועה's פתח is never fewer than seven clean days and never more than seventeen.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a woman who has lost track, the opening is never fewer than seven days and never more than seventeen days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the whole list in one rule. A טועה's clean-day count always falls between seven and seventeen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seventeen is the top of the list, for the shortest bleeding, and seven is the bottom, for the longest bleeding. This rule shows that the system has fixed limits on both ends. It is not an open-ended guess.

keyTerms.meaning: Fewer than seven
More than seventeen

steps.whatToRemember: A טועה's פתח is always somewhere from seven to seventeen clean days, depending on how many days she bled.

phrases.english: For there is no opening for a woman who has lost track
in fewer than seven,
and not in more than seventeen.
phrases.notes: He means clean days. The shortest bleeding needs the most clean days, and the longest bleeding needs the fewest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the list of individual cases into one general rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A טועה's פתח always ranges from seven to seventeen clean days.

steps.title: Why not just count seven clean days?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבה: why do we need this whole system? She could simply count seven clean days and be permitted to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבה: Why do I need all this? Let her count seven days and be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks the ברייתא's whole system, putting the question to רבה. This sets up the next move, where רבה will need to explain what his numbers are really for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether she is a נדה or a זבה, seven clean days is the most she ever needs to become permitted to her husband. So a count of eight, ten, or seventeen days seems pointless. The challenge pushes רבה to show that the count must serve some purpose other than permitting her to her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need all this? Used to challenge something as unnecessary
Let her count seven (clean days)
And she will be permitted (to her husband)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אדא is not saying the ברייתא's math is wrong. He is asking why the math is needed at all, if seven days already permits her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rabba:
Why do I need all of this?
Let her count seven and be permitted!
phrases.notes: He means seven clean days, after which she can go to the מקוה and be permitted to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the purpose of the entire counting system that was just summed up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's system of counting seven to seventeen clean days for a טועה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seven clean days is always enough to permit her, whether she is a נדה or a זבה. So any count longer than seven seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The counting is meant to fix her cycle, not to permit her to her husband
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the system of seven to seventeen clean days is not about permitting her to her husband. It is about setting her back on a clear נדה cycle so her uncertainty ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are talking about getting her set right regarding נדה, and about her פתח (her way out of uncertainty).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge from Step 3. Yes, she can count seven clean days and be with her husband, but that is not what this system is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא asked why we need a long system when seven clean days already permit her. רבה says the system has a different goal: to bring her back to a known cycle, so that future bleeding can be clearly labeled as נדה or זבה. Permission to her husband and fixing her cycle are two separate questions.

keyTerms.meaning: to set her right, to fix her status
a woman in her seven days of menstrual impurity
her 'opening': the point where her uncertainty is resolved

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבה is denying that seven clean days permit her to her husband. He agrees. He is saying the counting answers a different question.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבה is answering רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: To set her right regarding being a נדה
phrases.notes: He means getting her back into a clear cycle, so we know when her נדה days begin.

phrases.english: and her פתח is what we are talking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְתַקּוֹנַהּ לִידֵי נִדָּה וּפִתְחָהּ קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The counting system exists to permit her to her husband, so it seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The counting system exists to fix her נדה cycle and end her uncertainty, which seven clean days alone do not do.

steps.title: A ברייתא about uncertain women bringing a זבה's offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that uncertain women bring a זבה's קרבן, but it may not be eaten. The exceptions are the women whose פתח is seven or eight days; their קרבן is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: All women who are unsure are זבות. They bring a קרבן but it is not eaten, except for 'her פתח is seven' and 'her פתח is eight'. Those women bring a קרבן and it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא connected to the טועה cases from Steps 1 and 2. It sets out which uncertain women bring a קרבן that may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an uncertain woman brings the קרבן just in case, so the כהנים may not eat it. The ברייתא picks out two cases from the earlier ברייתא's list as exceptions: the woman with a seven-day פתח (thirteen days of bleeding) and the woman with an eight-day פתח (twelve days of bleeding). In those two cases her קרבן is fully valid and is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: women who are unsure (lost track of their cycle)
women who bled outside the נדה days, in the days of זיבה
the offering a זבה brings when she becomes pure
it is not eaten: it is brought because of the doubt, so the כהנים cannot eat it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All women who are unsure are זבות,
they bring an offering, and it is not eaten,
except for 'her פתח is seven'
phrases.notes: This is the woman from Step 1 who bled thirteen days.

phrases.english: and 'her פתח is eight',
phrases.notes: This is the woman from Step 1 who bled twelve days.

phrases.english: who bring an offering and it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא related to the earlier ברייתא's list of פתח cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uncertain women bring a זבה's קרבן that is not eaten, except the seven-day and eight-day פתח cases, where it is eaten.

steps.title: Two problems with the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks two questions. Are all uncertain women really זבות? And how can a woman who bled only one or two days bring a קרבן at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that all unsure women are זבות? And also, is a woman who bled one day or two days fit to bring a קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא from two directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First problem: an uncertain woman might be a נדה, so how can the ברייתא call her a זבה outright? Second problem: only a woman who bled three days in a row in the זיבה days brings a קרבן. Taken plainly, 'all unsure women' would include women who bled only one or two days, and they never bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say...? (introduces a question that rejects a reading)
and furthermore
someone fit (obligated) to bring an offering

phrases.english: Is that to say all unsure women are זבות?
And furthermore, one day or two days
is she fit to bring an offering?
phrases.notes: Only a זבה who bled three days in a row brings a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase כל הטועות זבות in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read plainly, the phrase calls every uncertain woman a זבה and includes women who bled one or two days. That contradicts both the doubt (she may be a נדה) and the rule that only a three-day זבה brings a קרבן.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: זבות who are unsure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the word order to 'all זבות who are unsure'. Now the ברייתא is talking only about women who bled three days and are unsure about their timing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: All זבות who are unsure bring a קרבן and it is not eaten, except 'her פתח is seven' and 'her פתח is eight', who bring a קרבן and it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both questions from Step 6 by rereading the ברייתא. The גמרא itself repeats the whole ברייתא with the new wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the words swapped, 'זבות' is the main group: women who bled three days in a row. That answers the one-day and two-day problem. 'Who are unsure' now describes their doubt about whether the bleeding fell in the נדה days or the זיבה days, instead of declaring them definite זבות. The two exceptions stay the same, and in those cases the קרבן is eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: rather: introduces a corrected reading
זבות who are unsure: women who bled three days but don't know if it was in the זיבה days

steps.whatToRemember: The uncertain זבה brings her קרבן because of the doubt, so it is not eaten. Only the women with a seven-day or eight-day פתח bring a קרבן that is eaten.
steps.confusionAlert: The only change is the order of two words: 'טועות זבות' becomes 'זבות הטועות'. The rest of the ברייתא stays exactly the same.

phrases.english: Rather: all זבות who are unsure
bring an offering, and it is not eaten,
except for 'her פתח is seven',
and 'her פתח is eight',
who bring an offering and it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenges of Step 6 by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls every uncertain woman a זבה, including women who bled only one or two days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks only of women who bled three days and are unsure whether it was in the זיבה days. Their קרבן is not eaten, except in the seven-day and eight-day פתח cases.

steps.title: Quarantine for leprous marks lasts one to three weeks
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets the limits: a quarantine for נגעים is never shorter than one week and never longer than three weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With leprous marks, there is no quarantine less than one week, and none more than three weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a minimum and a maximum for how long a person or thing with a נגע can be kept in quarantine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a כהן cannot decide right away whether a mark is impure, he puts it in quarantine (הסגר) and checks it again later. The משנה says the shortest quarantine is one week and the longest possible total is three weeks.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
Leprous marks (צרעת) on a person, clothing or house
A week (seven days)
Quarantine: setting the case aside to be checked again later

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean every quarantine lasts between one and three weeks for every kind of נגע. The גמרא will explain that the 'less than' part and the 'more than' part are talking about two different kinds of נגעים.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
With leprous marks there is no quarantine less than one week,
and none more than three weeks.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין בִּנְגָעִים פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁבוּעַ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It moves from the uncertain זבה cases in the earlier steps to the topic of נגעים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quarantine for נגעים is never less than one week and never more than three weeks in total.

steps.title: Minimum is for marks on a person, maximum is for marks on houses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'not less than a week' refers to נגעי אדם, and 'not more than three weeks' refers to נגעי בתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'Less than a week' refers to marks on a person. 'Not more than three weeks' refers to marks on houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which kind of נגע each half of the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two limits in the משנה come from two different areas. The one-week minimum is taught about נגעי אדם, marks on a person's body. The three-week maximum is taught about נגעי בתים, marks on a house, which can stay in quarantine longer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Leprous marks on a person's body
Leprous marks that appear on the walls of a house

phrases.english: Gemara:
"Less than a week"
refers to marks on a person,
and "not more than three weeks"
refers to marks on houses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which type of נגע each limit in the משנה is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one-week minimum is about נגעי אדם; the three-week maximum is about נגעי בתים.

steps.title: רב פפא links a פסוק in תהלים to the two kinds of marks
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads the first half of the פסוק, 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains', as נגעי אדם. He reads the second half, 'Your judgments are a great deep', as נגעי בתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains' refers to marks on a person. 'Your judgments are like the great deep' refers to marks on houses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a דרשה that connects the two kinds of נגעים from the משנה to the two halves of a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא matches the two halves of the פסוק to the two kinds of נגעים the גמרא just separated. Marks on a person match God's 'righteousness', and marks on houses match God's deep 'judgments'. This builds on the distinction from the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: Your righteousness or kindness (God's)
Like the mighty mountains
Your judgments
The great deep, an endless depth

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
"Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains"
these are marks on a person,
"Your judgments are like the great deep"
these are marks on houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא צִדְקָתְךָ כְּהַרְרֵי אֵל אֵלּוּ נִגְעֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the split between נגעי אדם and נגעי בתים by linking each one to half of a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'צדקתך כהררי אל' refers to נגעי אדם; 'משפטיך תהום רבה' refers to נגעי בתים.

steps.title: What is the plain meaning of the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this פסוק means on its simple level, apart from רב פפא's דרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The plain meaning of the verse — what is it talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the simple meaning of the פסוק, and two אמוראים will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's reading is a דרשה about נגעים. The גמרא now wants to know how the two halves of the פסוק connect in their plain sense: what does God's righteousness have to do with His deep judgments?

keyTerms.meaning: The plain, simple meaning of the פסוק
What is it written about?

phrases.english: The plain meaning of the verse — what is it talking about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's דרשה, the גמרא asks about the פסוק's simple meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the two halves of 'צדקתך כהררי אל, משפטיך תהום רבה' relate in the plain sense.

steps.title: רב יהודה: without God's kindness, no one could survive His judgment
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads the פסוק as one idea: if God's righteousness were not as great as mountains, no one could stand up to His judgments, which are as deep as the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If not for 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains', who could stand before 'Your judgments are like the great deep'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by joining the two halves of the פסוק into one sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, God's judgments are so deep and strict that no one could pass them. The first half of the פסוק, God's great kindness, is what saves people from that judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for
To stand before; to hold up against

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
If not for "Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains,"
who could stand before
"Your judgments are like the great deep"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אִלְמָלֵא צִדְקָתְךָ כְּהַרְרֵי אֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question about the פסוק's plain meaning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God's great kindness is what lets people survive His deep and strict judgment.

steps.title: רבה: God's kindness is great because His judgments are deep
steps.stepSummary: רבה reads the second half of the פסוק as the reason for the first: God's righteousness is like mighty mountains because His judgments are a great deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: 'Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains' because 'Your judgments are like the great deep.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a second, different reading of the plain meaning of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה read the פסוק as 'if not for A, who could survive B'. רבה reads it as 'A because of B'. The depth of God's judgment is the reason His kindness has to be so great.

keyTerms.meaning: Because

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's limits are one week minimum (נגעי אדם) and three weeks maximum (נגעי בתים). רב פפא ties these to the פסוק 'צדקתך כהררי אל, משפטיך תהום רבה'. In the plain meaning, רב יהודה says God's kindness lets us survive His judgment, and רבה says His kindness is great because His judgment is deep.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
"Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains"
because "Your judgments are like the great deep."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר צִדְקָתְךָ כְּהַרְרֵי אֵל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמִּשְׁפָּטֶיךָ תְּהוֹם רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, offering a different link between the two halves of the פסוק than רב יהודה's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second half explains the first: God's kindness is vast because His judgment is so deep.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying idea causes רב יהודה and רבה to read the פסוק differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what bigger idea is behind the two different readings of the פסוק from רב יהודה and רבה. This question sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 gave two readings of the same פסוק. Now the גמרא wants to know if the difference is just about wording or if it comes from a real difference in how they understand God's kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? A question asking for the root idea behind a dispute.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רב יהודה and רבה from the last two steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the underlying reason behind the two readings just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What deeper principle separates רב יהודה's reading from רבה's reading of the פסוק.

steps.title: The answer: an older dispute about hiding away or lifting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two readings follow a dispute between רבי אלעזר, who says God כובש (hides away), and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who says God נושא (lifts).
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about the dispute of רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, as it was taught: רבי אלעזר says God hides away; רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says God lifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to an older, already-known dispute. One sage says God hides away sins, the other says God lifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree that God is kind when He judges, but they picture it differently. רבי אלעזר says He presses down and hides some sins so they are not counted. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says He lifts the scale so that the person comes out well.

keyTerms.meaning: Presses down / hides away (God hides away some sins).
Lifts / carries (God lifts the scale in the person's favor).

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument about whether God is kind. Both sides agree He is. They only disagree about how His kindness works.

phrases.aramaic: בִּדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: In the dispute of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina,
as it was stated:
Rabbi Elazar says: He hides away,
phrases.notes: He means God hides away some of a person's sins so they don't get counted against him.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: נוֹשֵׂא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina says: He lifts.
phrases.notes: He means God lifts the scale so the person comes out ahead.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, דְּאִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by linking it to an earlier known dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two readings depend on whether God shows kindness by hiding away sins (רבי אלעזר) or by lifting (רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא).

steps.title: Matching each sage to each side
steps.stepSummary: רבה follows רבי אלעזר (hiding away), and רב יהודה follows רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא (lifting).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה holds like רבי אלעזר, and רב יהודה holds like רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by telling us which sage sides with which view. This closes the discussion of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said God's righteousness is great because His judgments are 'a great deep', so the sins are hidden away in the deep, like רבי אלעזר's כובש. רב יהודה said God's righteousness is high like mountains, so He lifts the person up, like רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's נושא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה = כובש (God hides sins away into the 'great deep'). רב יהודה = נושא (God lifts the person up, high as 'mighty mountains').

phrases.english: Rabba is like Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: and Rav Yehuda is like Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וְרַב יְהוּדָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by matching each later sage to one side of the older dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה's reading of the פסוק fits כובש; רב יהודה's reading fits נושא.

steps.title: New משנה: how many full months in a year
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a year has at least four full (30-day) months and should not have more than eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not have fewer than four full months in a year, and it did not seem right to have more than eight.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It continues the earlier pattern of 'not less than X and not more than Y', this time about the calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jewish months are either 29 days or 30 days (a 'full' month). The משנה sets a minimum of four full months a year and says more than eight did not seem right.

keyTerms.meaning: Full months, that have 30 days instead of 29.
We do not go below (a minimum).

phrases.english: MISHNA:
We do not have fewer than four months
that are full, in a year,
phrases.notes: A "full" month here has 30 days instead of 29. This is not about adding a leap month.

phrases.english: and it did not seem right to have more than eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵאַרְבָּעָה חֳדָשִׁים הַמְעוּבָּרִים בְּשָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the discussion of the פסוק ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year has at least four 30-day months and not more than eight.
steps.confusionAlert: מעוברים here does not mean a leap year with an extra month. It means a month that has 30 days.

steps.title: When the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are eaten
steps.stepSummary: The שתי הלחם are eaten on the second or third day after baking; the לחם הפנים is eaten on the ninth to eleventh day after baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two loaves are eaten no earlier than the second day and no later than the third. The לחם הפנים is eaten no earlier than the ninth day and no later than the eleventh.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with the same 'not less than, not more than' pattern, now about two kinds of bread in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both breads are baked some days before they are eaten. The משנה gives the shortest and longest time that can pass between baking and eating for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought in the בית המקדש on שבועות.
The shewbread placed on the שולחן in the בית המקדש each שבת.
More than (a maximum).

phrases.english: The two loaves are not eaten
before the second day,
phrases.notes: Counting from when they were baked.

phrases.english: and not after the third.
The shewbread is not eaten
before the ninth day,
and not after the eleventh.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם אֵין נֶאֱכָלִין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה's list of minimums and maximums.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שתי הלחם: eaten on day 2 to 3 after baking. לחם הפנים: eaten on day 9 to 11 after baking.

steps.title: When a baby boy has his מילה
steps.stepSummary: A baby boy is not circumcised before the eighth day and not after the twelfth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baby boy is not circumcised before the eighth day, and not after the twelfth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its list with ברית מילה: it can be no earlier than day eight and, in normal cases of delay, no later than day twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day eight is the normal day. The משנה is telling us that even when things like שבת or יום טוב push off the מילה, the latest it ever reaches in these cases is day twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor; here, a newborn baby boy.
Is circumcised (has his ברית מילה).

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list of ranges: full months 4 to 8; שתי הלחם day 2 to 3; לחם הפנים day 9 to 11; מילה day 8 to 12.

phrases.english: A baby boy is not circumcised before the eighth day,
and not after the twelfth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last item to the משנה's list of minimum and maximum days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is done no earlier than day 8 and no later than day 12.

steps.title: What does 'it did not seem more than eight' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה means when it says 'it did not seem' right to have more than eight full months.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does the משנה mean by 'it did not seem more than eight'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section starts here. It asks what the unclear wording of the משנה from Step 17 means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא נראה' are vague. They do not say who it did not seem right to, or what exactly was not done more than eight times. The גמרא wants the full meaning spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: It did not seem right; it was not considered proper

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the meaning of
phrases.notes: This is the משנה from Step 17, which said a year should not have more than eight full months.

phrases.english: 'It did not seem more than eight'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לֹא נִרְאָה יָתֵר עַל שְׁמֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the משנה quoted in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who did it not seem right to, and what exactly should not go past eight?

steps.title: רב הונא: The חכמים did not want more than eight full months
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the חכמים did not think it proper to make more than eight months of the year full (30 days).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The Sages did not think it proper to make more than eight months full.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. It was the חכמים who did not think it right to make more than eight months full in one year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא fills in the missing pieces. 'It did not seem' means 'it did not seem right to the חכמים.' 'More than eight' means more than eight full, 30-day months.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who set up the calendar
Here: to make a month full by giving it 30 days

steps.confusionAlert: Here לְעַבֵּר does not mean adding a leap month to the year. It means making a single month full, with 30 days instead of 29.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
It did not seem proper to the Sages
to make more than eight months full.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא לֹא נִרְאָה לַחֲכָמִים לְעַבֵּר יָתֵר עַל שְׁמוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים did not think it proper to make more than eight months of the year full (30 days).

steps.title: Why not nine full months?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is wrong with nine full months, since the חכמים would not allow that many.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about nine, that the Sages did not allow it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the limit is eight, the גמרא asks for the reason. Why is nine not allowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא only explained what the rule means, not why it exists. Eight seems like a random number, so the גמרא asks what problem would come up with a ninth full month.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why is this case treated differently?

phrases.english: What is different about nine, that it is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב הונא's explanation by asking for the reason behind the limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What problem would happen if nine months were made full?

steps.title: The answer begins: 'If so'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with 'אם כן' (if so). The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain the problem with nine full months. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אם כן' means 'if that were done.' It sets up a problem that would happen if nine months were full. The problem itself is stated in the continuation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that were the case

phrases.english: If so,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the opening 'if so' appears here. The actual reason continues in the following text.
